Page iii
Introduction
This
document
is
the
user
guide
of
the
REST
API
for
Product
Usage
Management.
It
includes the data model definition as well as all available operations for the ProductUsage
resource.
The
Product
Usage
Management
API
provides
a
standardized
mechanism
for
Product
Usage
management
such
as
the
creation,
update,
retrieval
of
a
Product
Usage
or
of
a
collection of Product Usage.
A Product Usage entity represents the structured report of a service that has been delivered,
guided to a product, used and is considered billable. Each Product Usage entity is defined
by
a
corresponding
Product
Usage
Specification,
which
standardizes
what
type
of
usage
occurred
(e.g.,
voice,
data
session,
API
call)
and
its
associated
characteristics
(e.g.,
duration, data consumption, correlation identifier). The main content of a Product Usage is a
list of characteristics (name-value pairs), that are needed to guide and/or to rate the usage.
For
example, A
and
B
numbers
in
a
telephone
call,
amount
of
data
transferred
in
a
data
packet transfer, etc. Other key attributes of Product Usage are its id, creation date, status
and the id of the related product and of the related Product Usage Specification.
TMF767
Product
Usage
Catalog
Management
API
is
responsible
for
managing
Product
Usage
Specifications
that
represents
a
catalog
view
of
the
targeted
Product
Usage
comprised
of
characteristics
specifications
which
define
all
the
attributes
known
for
the
particular usage.
The Product Usage API manages both rated and non-rated usages. For example, it allows a
service provider:
•
To retrieve usage generated by a partner platform in order to rate it
•
To provide rated usages to a partner for their consumption
A ProductUsage represents an entity that may be of interest to the business and can have
charges applied to it. It is comprised of characteristics which define all the attributes known
for
that
particular
type
of
usage. The
main
attributes
are
its
id,
creationDate,
usageType,
related UsageSpecification, characteristics (name/value pairs), status, price charged (date,
amount, taxes), product involved in the usage. A ProductUsage follows a simple life cycle
which is presented in the following chapter 'ProductUsage life cycle'.
The Product Usage API exposes the following operations on the ProductUsage resource:
•
Creation of a ProductUsage. Note that creation of a ProductUsage can be done without
the API, rather as the result of internal processing by an online charging system or policy
control system
•
Retrieval of a ProductUsage or a collection of ProductUsage, depending on filter criteria
•
Partial update of a ProductUsage or of a collection of ProductUsage
•
Deletion of a ProductUsage
The Product Usage API also optionally exposes the ExportJob resource:
•
An ExportJob represents a task used to export productUsage representations.
Product Usage Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 1
•
To trigger the export of productUsage, an ExportJob is created by the API client using
POST operation on the ExportJob resource.
•
The ExportJob is then processed by the API server, which generates a file containing the
productUsage representations and stores it in a designated location.
•
The API client can then retrieve the ExportJob status and the generated file using the
GET operation on the ExportJob resource.
•
The ExportJob can be used to export productUsage representations in various formats,
such as JSON or CSV.
•
The
ExportJob
resource
allows
the
API
client
to
specify
the
filter
criteria
for
the
productUsage
representations
to
be
exported,
such
as
creationDate
range,
status,
related product.id.
•
An
ExportJob
follows
a
simple
life
cycle
which
is
presented
in
the
following
chapter
'ExportJob life cycle'.
The Product Usage API exposes the following operations on the ExportJob resource:
•
Creation of an ExportJob
•
Retrieval of an ExportJob or a collection of ExportJob, depending on filter criteria
•
Deletion of an ExportJob

initialized

The product, customer billing account and pricing

The ProductUsage has been rated, at least one
product price has been created
(usageProductPrice) within the ProductUsage
corrected
The ProductUsage is resubmitted after error
correction
superseded
This ProductUsage record has been superseded
by another due to error (e.g., wrong price) and is
no longer billable
notRated
The ProductUsage has not been rated, due to
business rules (e.g., no price applicable for this
usage type)
failed
The ProductUsage record has been validated but
rating failed

Page 4
The ExportJob task can be either:
•
short-running task, where the result of the task can be returned in the same call to the
client
•
long-running
task,
where
the
result
cannot
be
computed
immediately;
then
the
task
resource can be created and returned to the client in the same API call
When an implementation for a Task supports both alternatives, it MAY decide at runtime to
execute
the
task
as
short-running
or
long-running
task,
taking
into
consideration
its
expectation of the duration of task execution, e.g. by investigating any request parameters or
payload values.
In that case, the consumer must be able to distinguish and handle both variants of the task
operation.
Refer to TMF630 REST guidelines for more details on Task pattern.

in Product Usage ABE as ProductUsage entity.

Information Framework excerpts:
Put simply, usage is how much service is used, by whom is it used, where and when is it used and circumstances
under which it is used.
The ProductUsage describes the usage of an instantiated Product.
Note that the API representation of Information Framework model is partial. In particular the
direct
relationship
between
a
ProductUsage
(that
would
be
originated
from
a
ResourceUsage)
and
a
ResourceUsage
is
not
implemented
for
now
because
of
lack
of
business need for this.
Note that Information Framework and API specification may evolve independently but tend
to be consistent as much as possible.

Sample Use Cases
The examples in this User Guide and OAS file come from the TMFS005 Use Case Billing
Fiber Contract and TMFS009 Use Case Usage and Balance Management documents.
•
Creation of a simple ProductUsage relating to a completed and rated voice call retrieval
•
listing ProductUsage of usageType “InternationalVoice”
•
retrieving a specific ProductUsage based on its id
•
updating a Product Usage status to "recycled"
Note that entities and characteristic names don’t always fully match but the meaning should
match.

Export
Using ExportJob, the ProductUsage can be exported to a file.
Note
:
an
implementation
of
this API
could
expose
only
exportJob
resource
if
it’s
agreed
between
API
client
and
API
server
that
the
exportJob
is
the
only
way
to
retrieve
ProductUsage (indivivual GET queries of productUsage not allowed). This can be useful for
performance reasons, e.g. if the producUsage are of a high number and/or if the interface
explicitely allows only 1 single mechanism to retrieve the productUsage entities for simplicity
reasons.

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a StringCharacteristic
and BooleanCharacteristic inheriting properties from the abstract Characteristic entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
a
list
of
Characteristic
instances
some
may
be
instances
of
StringCharacteristic
where
other
could
be
instances
of
BooleanCharacteristic.
The
@type
gives
this
information. All
resources
and
sub-resources
of
the
Product
Usage API
have
a
@type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.
The
@referredType
can
be
used
within
reference
entities
(like
for
instance
a
ProductUsageSpecificationtRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type of the reference itself, such as ProductUsageSpecificationtRef, and not the class type of
the
referred
object.
However
since
reference
classes
are
rarely
sub-classed,
@type
is
generally not useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

Page 14
usageCharacteristic
A Characteristic. Characteristics of product usage. Each
characteristic should correspond to a characteristic specification
described in the corresponding product usage specification.
Characteristic can be instantiated as
* BooleanArrayCharacteristic
* BooleanCharacteristic
* FloatArrayCharacteristic
* FloatCharacteristic
* IntegerArrayCharacteristic
* IntegerCharacteristic
* NumberArrayCharacteristic
* NumberCharacteristic
* ObjectArrayCharacteristic
* ObjectCharacteristic
* StringArrayCharacteristic
* StringCharacteristic
usageProductPrice
A ProductPrice. Price assigned to the product usage when
product usage is rated. The price should be valued without
applied taxes (dutyFreeAmount), that permits to avoid loss of
precision. Better precision is reached by applying taxes on the
total dutyFreeAmount of several Product Usage Price. Note that
in this API the recurringChargePeriod attribute is not applicable.
usageSpecification
A ProductUsageSpecificationRef. ProductUsageSpecification
reference. ProductUsageSpecification is a detailed description of
a product usage event that are of interest to the business and
can have charges applied to it. It is comprised of characteristics,
which define all attributes known for a particular type of usage.
usageType
A String. This attribute can be used to precise the type of usage,
for instance in the case 1 single ProductUsageSpecification
manages different types of usages.

ExportJob resource
Represents a task used to export resources to a file.
Resource model
Product Usage Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 26
Figure 3 - ExportJob
Field descriptions
ExportJob fields
completionDate
A DateTime. Data at which the job was completed.
contentType
A String. The format of the exported data. This value should be
according to the IANA standard list of media types. Default is
'application/json'.
creationDate
A DateTime. Date at which the job was created.
errorLog
A String. Path to file or stream where errors encountered during
the job processing can be written.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
path
A String. A Json Pointer or a Json Path relative to the API root
node that points to the resource acting as the source for
streaming content to the export destination specified by the
ExportJob. Defaults to the API?s root node. Using the JSON
Pointer resp. JSON Path with reference to the API root
guarantees that the path cannot point to a resource outside the
scope of this API, e.g. to export some resource managed by a
different API.
query
A String. Used to scope the exported data. Identical to GET filter
construct using the API?s node defined by path as base.
Defaults to requesting all resources of the node defined by the
path.
Product Usage Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 27
status
A JobStateType. Valid values for the state of a batch job (e.g.
catalog import). ENUMERATED with values:
* Not Started
* Running
* Succeeded
* Failed
url
A Uri. URL pointing at the location for the exported file. The URL
sould be of the form
file://host/path
where host is the fully
qualified domain name of the system on which the path is
accessible, and path is a hierarchical directory path of the form
directory/directory/??/name. Other schemes can also be
supported, e.g. 'ftp' and 'http', preferably with their TLS encrypted
variants 'sftp' resp 'https'.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample
REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls
will
be
rejected
by
the
service
if
it
does
not
support
multiple
listeners.
In
this
case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
 
"id":"42",
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com",
 
"query":""
}
Product Usage Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 54
Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.
Request
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
Response
204
Publish Event to listener
POST /client/listener
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE”
should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification
resources
Models
section)
and
EVENT
BODY
refers
to
the
data
structure
of
the
given
notification type.
Request
Product Usage Management User Guide

Page 55
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
 
"event": {
 
EVENT BODY
 
},
 
"eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
Response
201

Release Notes
V4.0.0 vs v5.0.0
general changes
•
common changes due to v5 tooling assets (OAS, User Guide, Conformance Profile…)
generation
•
usageSpecification
endpoint
removed,
moved
to
TMF767
Product
Usage
Catalog
Management API, same for usageSpecification related events
•
endpoint
/usage
renamed
into
/productUsage.
Note
that
serviceUsage
and
resourceUsage endpoints are managed in specific API TMF727 and TMF771
•
usageXXX events removed (no more events)
•
productUsage lifecycle changed to fit better the usage definition in Product domain
•
addition
of
/exportJob
resource
to
allow
export
of
product
usage
data
in
a
file,
and
exportJob events to receive corresponding notifications
•
User Guide updated with excerpts from Information Framework and TMFS005 Use Case
•
Conformance Profile updated accordingly to these changes
schemas changes
•
productUsage : usageDate renamed into creationDate to follow general guidelines
•
productUsage : lastUpdate added to have the latest update date of the product usage
•
productUsage : externalIdentifier added to allow an array of external identifiers related to
the product usage
•
productUsage : status changed from enum to open string with enum proposal to allow
more flexibility
•
productUsage
:
usageCharacteristic
uses
generic
Characteristic
schema
instead
of
UsageCharacteristic schema, to follow general guidelines
•
productUsage
:
serviceUsage
added
to
give
the
identifier
of
the
service
usage(s)
that
participated in the creation of the product usage
•
productUsage
:
relatedParty
uses
RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef
schema
instead
of
RelatedParty schema to follow general guidelines
•
productUsage : ratedProductUsage renamed into usageProductPrice to express this is a
price
•
productUsage
:
usageProductPrice
uses
common
schema
ProductPrice
instead
of
RatedProductUsage schema
•
productUsage
:
product
reference
is
in
the
productUsage
root
instead
of
being
in
the
usage price attribute for better clarity
•
